messages:
maria: Heads up — noticed a host-side preproc perf regression after the 03:12 deploy, affects tokenization + streaming chunking paths. p95 decode latency went from ~45ms to ~120ms on small prompt workloads.
li: ugh. any obvious spike in CPU or syscalls?
maria: CPU user+sys up ~2x on the ingress proxy (see snapshot). grpc writev rate also spiked. KV cache hit-rate dropped 92% -> 68% for a particular hot-prefix.
jonathan: did kernel selection change? logs show a fallback path. sample from logs: `selected_kernel=matmul_f32 fallback=matmul_int8_unfused reason=quant-unfriendly`
maria: yea that's what I saw. also batching heuristics started flushing earlier — median batch size down 12 -> 3, so we lost batch amortization.
sam: can you paste the perf-ci flame?
perf-ci: [automated] host-preproc/job/1818202020/flame.svg uploaded (1.2MB)
maria: uploaded to the thread but TL;DR flame shows hot in parse/tokenizer::emit_slab and grpc::writev_coalesce.
li: hypothesis: a minor change to streaming framing caused more fragmentation, which both trips the batching threshold and causes KV cache prefix mismatch. if slab keys included window offsets, we could be invalidating more frequently.
jonathan: good call. putting together a small repro: run `./bench_ingress --seq 32 --qps 500 --streaming` and trace KV key churn. expecting eviction rate spike.
maria: repro confirms eviction spike. repro logs: `kvcache.evictions=612/s` vs baseline `45/s`.
sam: can we mitigate quickly? options: relax early-flush heuristics, disable the new framing change, or patch kernel selector to prefer fused kernels even with partial quantization.
jonathan: short-term I'll revert the framing change in canary and run a 2hr soak. li, can you bisect the framing commit to the exact diff that added the offset to slab keys?
li: on it. bisect started -> suspect commit 0aef3b9 (adds window_offset to slab key).
perf-ci: regression alert pinned to commit 0aef3b9 (host-proxy framing).
maria: devx-bot, add a dashboard panel for kvcache.evictions and batch_size distribution for the next deploy.
devx-bot: created issue #2341 and dashboard panel 'host-preproc-kv-evictions' (linked).
jonathan: patch ready to revert offset change, smoke passed locally. scheduling canary at 15:10 PT.
li: bisect confirmed 0aef3b9. we'll patch to keep offset out of key and instead include it in metadata to avoid eviction churn.
sam: longer-term: we should also make kernel selector cost-aware of batch-size drop so it doesn't pick quantized unfused kernels at small batch sizes (they lose perf). filing a follow-up RFC.
maria: agreed. next steps: 1) canary revert 15:10, 2) li deploy key-patch if canary green, 3) jonathan RFC for kernel selector heuristics, 4) sam adds automated regression test for kvcache eviction delta.
jonathan: thumbs up. I'll post canary results in 15:40. :eyes:
li: I have a local patch that keeps key stable and adds a histogram metric for key-versions. pushing after canary.
maria: thanks all. saved the flame images + heap snapshots to the incident folder: https://redwood.internal/ops/incidents/1818202020-host-preproc.
sam: nice triage. :thumbsup:
jonathan: canary looks good — p95 back to ~50ms, eviction rate back to baseline. rolling to prod.
maria: prod roll complete, metrics look stable now. leaving this open for postmortem notes.
li: will draft postmortem and include microbench numbers + kernel selection test.
maria: amazing work. closing loop once PM doc is up. :party:
